observation.visible_scene: Two adjacent concrete surfaces fill the frame: a pale gray, pebbled slab on the left and a smoother reddish-pink slab on the right, divided by a roughly vertical seam. A long dark shadow of a person lies diagonally across both slabs, with the rounded head/shoulder portion on the gray side and the legs/feet extending toward the upper-right on the red side. A thin, straight, pole- or wire-like shadow crosses the upper portion of the scene.
visible_changes: The thin straight shadow enters as a faint line at the top-left edge and progressively sweeps downward and rightward, by mid-to-late excerpt crossing the seam and overlapping the person's torso shadow.
The vertical seam and the person's shadow both drift leftward within the frame over the sequence, indicating camera translation/pan across the ground.

The person's shadow silhouette changes subtly in shape (a small arm/hand-like protrusion appears near the torso in several later frames), consistent with the person moving, though the limb motion is not clearly resolved.
outside_clip_unknowns: What object casts the thin straight shadow (pole, wire, or other) is not visible.
Whether the shadow shifts are due to the person walking, the sun moving, or camera motion is not determinable from this excerpt alone.
The onset and completion of any walking or shadow movement lie outside the cropped segment.
uncertain_details: The relative contribution of camera pan versus physical shadow movement cannot be separated because the ground texture is uniform.
The exact pose or gait of the person is inferred only from shadow outline changes and remains uncertain.
